sh: Huge Prague rally to defend public media
headline: Hundreds of thousands rally in Prague against the government’s plan for public TV and radio
summary: A very large crowd gathered in Prague on Sunday 15 November to oppose Prime Minister Andrej Babiš’s plan to change how public TV and radio are funded. Media estimates put the crowd at 350,000 to 400,000.
why: Critics fear the plan would make public broadcasters depend on the government and weaken their independence. The rally also turned into a wider protest against the Babiš government.

event.t: The rally took place on Letná, Prague’s largest open space. Media estimates put the crowd at 350,000 to 400,000 people.
The government plans to abolish the licence fee and pay for public TV and radio from the state budget.
Protesters say the change would weaken the independence of the broadcasters. Many also criticised how the government handled the law in parliament.
Staff at Czech public TV and radio went on strike on 3 November against the plan.

effects.label: Czech Television and Czech Radio
effects.t: Their money would come from the state budget instead of a fee paid by households.

effects.label: Babiš government
effects.t: Faces growing street pressure over the law.
